findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: Home to School Transport continues to escalate structurally, with no end to demand growth in sight.
findings.detail: Home to School Transport overspend increased by a further £139k in 2025/26, continuing a pattern of uncontrolled growth. The report attributes this to 'increased demand and the costs associated with placements, such as passenger assistants and general route costs from the supplier.' This is an ongoing structural problem that appeared to have no mitigation in the year-end position.
findings.matters: This is a recurring overspend in a growing area (demand-driven by SEND placement growth and transport costs). If demand continues to rise and costs escalate with provider pricing, this could become a material recurring pressure.
findings.figures: £139k further overspend in 2025/26; driven by combination of increased demand and placement costs
findings.quote: The expenditure on Home to School transport continued to increase by a further £139,000. This was driven by a combination of increased demand and the costs associated with placements, such as passenger assistants and general route costs from the supplier.

findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: General Fund Balance remains inadequate at £8m, only 3% of planned 5% requirement by 2028/29.
findings.detail: The council's General Fund Balance has remained static at £8m since 2022/23, despite agreed plans to increase it by £1m per annum to reach £11m by 2028/29. The council's own financial policy states it should hold 5% of Net Revenue Expenditure in General Fund Balance (estimated at £15.6m by 2028/29), leaving a significant adequacy gap. This constrains the council's financial flexibility to manage further demand shocks.
findings.matters: Inadequate reserves relative to budget volatility and the scale of demand-driven pressures (Children's Social Care, SEND, Adult Social Care) increase refinance and service delivery risk. A council with 3% of reserves against a 5% policy target and facing £18m budget gaps has limited buffer for shocks.
findings.figures: Current balance £8m; target £11m by 2028/29; policy requirement £15.6m (5% of NRE) by 2028/29; current level represents 3% of estimated NRE
findings.quote: The Council's general fund balance has remained at £8m since 2022/23... the Council should aim to hold 5% of Net Revenue Expenditure in General Fund balances, this is estimated to be £15.6m by 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: Severe budget gaps ahead: £6.7m in 2026/27 rising to £18.4m by 2028/29.
findings.detail: The budget report identified substantial gaps: £6.7m in 2026/27, £13.8m in 2027/28, and £18.4m in 2028/29. The council is pursuing transformation reviews (Powering our Futures programme) but has not yet detailed how these gaps will be closed. The report acknowledges ongoing pressures in Children's Social Care, Adult Social Care, Home to School Transport, and SEND.
findings.matters: The scale and trajectory of these gaps raises questions about service sustainability without either significant borrowing, reserve drawdown, or council tax increases. A lender needs to understand the council's credible plan to address these gaps.
findings.quote: there is an estimated budget gap of £6.7m in 2026/27, rising to £13.8m in 2027/28 and £18.4m in 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: Transformation savings programme fell £700k short, reducing the council's ability to offset demand pressures.
findings.detail: The council recorded a £700k shortfall against planned transformation savings. This savings shortfall contributed directly to the overall overspend and signals that the council's efficiency programme is not delivering at planned pace. No detail is provided on which savings failed to materialise.
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence that the council can deliver its own transformation plan to bridge the growing budget gap (£6.7m to £18.4m over the MTFP). A savings shortfall in an already overspending year suggests execution risk in the medium-term financial plan.
findings.figures: £700k shortfall recorded in revenue outturn table
findings.quote: Transformation Savings Shortfall 0  700  700  700  0

findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit has ballooned to £17.135m, nearly triple from the previous year.
findings.detail: The DSG deficit grew from £6.72m at 31 March 2025 to £17.135m at 31 March 2026—a £10.4m in-year overspend. The High Needs Block alone overspent by £11.5m, driven by £3.7m from independent school placements and £2.3m from other LA school placements. While a statutory override exists until March 2028, the council must fund 10% of the deficit (£1.7m set aside) from its own reserves.
findings.matters: A growing DSG deficit is a material contingent liability. Even with the statutory override, the council is committing reserve resources to cover the 10% it cannot recover from government. The trajectory—nearly £3.5m worse than Q3 forecast in the final quarter alone—suggests the underlying drivers (SEND placement growth) are not stabilising.
findings.figures: £17.135m cumulative deficit; £10.4m in-year overspend; £11.5m High Needs Block overspend; £1.7m set aside from reserves for 10% residual liability
findings.quote: The cumulative DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 is now £17.135m... Increase in number and cost of placements in Independent Schools (£3.7m) and in other LA schools/academies (£2.3m).

findings.paper_title: MTFP 2526 Outturn Report
findings.headline: Children's Social Care overspent by £4.123m with escalating external placement costs.
findings.detail: The directorate overspent by £4.123m, driven primarily by external residential placements rising by a further £1.3m in the final quarter alone. The report attributes this to increased demand, fee increases from providers, and greater support requirements. This represents a material failure to control a demand-driven budget.
findings.matters: This is the largest single directorate overspend and signals that planned controls on Children's Social Care costs are not working. The council is repeatedly experiencing late-year escalations in this budget, indicating difficulty forecasting or managing provider costs.
findings.figures: £4.123m directorate overspend; £1.3m further overspend in final quarter; external residential placements increased
findings.quote: There has been an increase in children in external residential placements since December, as well as additional cost pressures on placements due to fee increases and greater support requirements, this has led to a further overspend at the year end of £1,300,000.

findings.paper_title: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council 2025-26 Audit Strategy Memorandum FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Hampton by Hilton Hotel valuation subject to significant judgment and comprises the largest balance in investment property
findings.detail: The auditor has identified the valuation of the Council's investment property, specifically the Hampton by Hilton Hotel, as a significant audit risk. This property is the Council's largest investment and its valuation involves significant judgment, estimation uncertainty, and assumptions about market conditions. The auditor will engage specialists to assess the valuer's assumptions and the appropriateness of valuation methodology.
findings.matters: A large investment property valuation subject to significant judgment could materially misstate the council's balance sheet and assets available for borrowing. Hotel valuations are volatile and sensitive to market conditions.
findings.figures: Hampton by Hilton is the largest balance within investment property (specific value not disclosed)
findings.quote: The Council obtains a specialist valuation of its largest investment, the Hampton by Hilton Hotel. The scope of our valuations work will therefore also include the hotel valuation which is the largest balance within investment property.

findings.paper_title: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council 2025-26 Audit Strategy Memorandum FINAL - signed
findings.headline: New children's mental health and behavioural distress homes approved but expected to deliver no savings beyond running costs
findings.detail: The Council has approved creation of two new SBC homes for children with mental health and behavioural distress. The auditor explicitly notes these are 'not expected to deliver any savings beyond those needed to fund the running costs of the homes and associated borrowing'. The homes will provide stable placements and represent additional ongoing expenditure requiring borrowing.
findings.matters: Capital projects that require ongoing subsidy rather than generating cost savings add to long-term revenue pressure at a time when the council is struggling to balance its budget.
findings.figures: Two new homes; additional borrowing required for construction and associated running costs
findings.quote: The creation of two new SBC homes for Children with Mental Health and Behavioural distress is not expected to deliver any savings beyond those needed to fund the running costs of the homes and associated borrowing.

findings.paper_title: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council 2025-26 Audit Strategy Memorandum FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Adult and Children's services overspends requiring £9.9m in savings to avoid further reserve depletion
findings.detail: The Council's 'Powering Our Future Programme' has identified up to £9.9m of savings needed to address Adult and Children's services overspends, with the majority planned for 2025/26. Reserves have been decreasing over recent years, and the auditor notes that achieving these savings is critical to avoid further reserve depletion. The new fostering model, approved in July 2025, is identified as the most critical intervention to address cost pressures.
findings.matters: Declining reserves combined with unresolved service overspends indicates structural budget problems. Failure of the £9.9m programme would force further reserve use or service reductions.
findings.figures: £9.9m savings target identified; reserves have been decreasing over recent years
findings.quote: It is critical that the Council deliver these savings to avoid further reliance on Council reserves which have been decreasing over recent years.

findings.paper_title: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council 2025-26 Audit Strategy Memorandum FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit forecast to reach £35m by 2027/28 with statutory override expiring in 2028
findings.detail: The Council reported a cumulative DSG deficit of £6m as at 31 March 2025, forecasted to reach £35m by 2027/28 without mitigations. The statutory override allowing ring-fencing from the general fund is intended to expire on 31 March 2028. Without successful delivery of the Delivering Better Value (DBV) plan, the Council risks being unable to set a balanced budget in 2028/29 when this amount would need to be absorbed.
findings.matters: A £35m structural deficit requiring absorption into the general fund balance would represent an existential threat to the council's financial sustainability and borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: £6m cumulative deficit at 31 March 2025; £35m forecast by 2027/28 without mitigations; statutory override expires 31 March 2028
findings.quote: without action to address the cumulative deficit, at the end of this period there is a risk that the Council will be unable to set a balanced budget

findings.paper_title: Audit & Gov Committee draft AGS 25 26 Report
findings.headline: Capital project delivery at risk from insufficient workforce capacity
findings.detail: A scrutiny review of capital project governance found the arrangements in place since November 2024 provided a solid foundation but explicitly highlighted the need to ensure sufficient skills and capacity to deliver the programme. The council is addressing this through development of a People Plan and improved communication of risk and lessons learnt, but capacity constraints are flagged as a risk to delivery.
findings.matters: If the council lacks sufficient workforce to execute its capital programme, this could delay schemes, affect financial performance, and impact borrowing requirements.
findings.quote: The need to ensure sufficient skills and capacity to deliver the programme was also highlighted and Members were made aware of the development of the Council's workforce "People Plan".

findings.paper_title: June 2026 - Internal Audit Annual Report
findings.headline: Two audit recommendations remain unimplemented past their originally agreed implementation dates
findings.detail: Management has not implemented two audit recommendations within the timeframe originally outlined. While the report describes management as generally responsive to audit findings, these outstanding items represent a control weakness where identified issues have not been remedied.
findings.matters: Unimplemented audit recommendations signal that identified control deficiencies remain unremedied, which weakens confidence in the control environment.
findings.figures: 2 recommendations
findings.quote: Management continue to engage positively with Audit recommendations with only 2 recommendations not implemented within the timeframe originally outlined.

findings.paper_title: 08 SBC- Audit Completion Report 24-25 FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Material PPE valuation adjustments and prior-year control gaps in fixed asset register suggest ongoing asset accounting weaknesses
findings.detail: The council identified several material PPE misstatements in 2024/25: £1.7m unadjusted accrual not provided; £1.059m Norton Town Centre misclassification; £1.636m investment property reclassification. Audit findings from prior years noted that the Fixed Asset Register contained assets no longer in existence and multiple misstatements in asset movements. While the council has committed to a comprehensive FAR review, these issues signal control weaknesses around asset recording and valuation.
findings.matters: PPE is material to the balance sheet. Repeated adjustments and control gaps increase audit risk and suggest potential for undetected misstatement.
findings.figures: Unadjusted: £1,702k; Adjusted: £709k, £1,059k, £1,636k
findings.quote: From our cut-off testing, we found that one accrual was not provided for at the 31 March 2025. The figure reported is the extrapolated impact.

findings.paper_title: 08 SBC- Audit Completion Report 24-25 FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Finance team struggled with IFRS 16 implementation, requiring four separate draft iterations over nine months
findings.detail: IFRS 16 Leases was a new standard for the council in 2024/25. Draft accounts submitted on 27 June 2025 contained incomplete disclosures and were non-compliant. Technical review identified that half of all audit comments related to IFRS 16. Updated drafts were required in September 2025, January 2026, and February 2026. Management attributed this to 'extremely tight deadline to produce draft accounts by the end of June 2025.'
findings.matters: Multiple iterations and attribution to tight timelines signal capacity or capability constraints within the finance function. This increases risk of future material misstatements, particularly on complex accounting areas.
findings.figures: Draft dates: 27 June 2025; 13 February 2026; audit work ongoing through 19 February 2026
findings.quote: Due to the extremely tight deadline to produce draft accounts by the end of June 2025 there was insufficient time to produce all relevant calculations and produce all relevant disclosure notes which were applicable when adopting the new standard for the first year in 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: 08 SBC- Audit Completion Report 24-25 FINAL - signed
findings.headline: £8.1m savings programme from Powering Our Future is critical to avoid further reserve dependence, with new fostering model flagged for required monitoring
findings.detail: The Powering Our Future Programme has identified up to £8.1m of potential savings opportunities. Most are planned for 2025/26 onwards. The new fostering model, approved by Cabinet in July 2025, is identified as 'the most critical in addressing cost pressures and will require monitoring.' The auditor explicitly states these savings are critical to avoid further reliance on reserves.
findings.matters: Savings remain aspirational until delivered. The flagging of the new fostering model for 'required monitoring' indicates execution risk. If the programme falters or if the critical fostering model does not deliver as expected, the council will accelerate reserve depletion and face budget deficits.
findings.figures: up to £8.1m of savings identified; new fostering model approved July 2025; majority of savings planned 2025/26 onwards
findings.quote: It is critical that the Council deliver these savings to avoid further reliance on Council reserves which have been decreasing over recent years.

findings.paper_title: 08 SBC- Audit Completion Report 24-25 FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Council is managing ongoing revenue overspend through reserve drawdown, with reserves decreasing over recent years
findings.detail: The council projected an overspend of £6.6m for 2024/25 (as of December 2024 update). This continues a pattern of overspending identified in prior year audits. The auditor notes that reserves have been decreasing over recent years and is managing through reserve depletion rather than bringing expenditure into line with budget.
findings.matters: Declining reserves limit the council's financial resilience to manage unexpected shocks or shortfalls. Persistent overspend suggests underlying structural imbalances or spending control issues.
findings.figures: £6.6m projected overspend; reserves decreasing over recent years
findings.quote: From the latest update in December 2024, the Council projected an overspend of £6.6m.

findings.paper_title: 08 SBC- Audit Completion Report 24-25 FINAL - signed
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit forecast to reach £35m by 2027/28 when statutory override ends
findings.detail: The council has a cumulative DSG deficit of £6.725m as at 31 March 2025, which is ring-fenced from the general fund under statutory override. However, this override is due to end on 31 March 2028. Without the Council's Delivering Better Value plan, the deficit is forecast to reach £35m by 2027/28. The auditor explicitly states: 'It is critical that the Council deliver its Delivering Better Value plan to ensure the cumulative deficit is reduced at the point the statutory override ends in 2028.'
findings.matters: This creates a structural deficit that will become a general fund obligation in 2028/29. If the DBV plan does not deliver, the council faces an unmanageable budget gap and potential inability to set a balanced budget.
findings.figures: cumulative DSG deficit of £6.725m as at 31 March 2025; forecasted to reach £35m by 2027/28; statutory override ends 31 March 2028
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2025 the Council's DSG shows a cumulative deficit balance of £6m, which is forecasted to reach £35m by 2027/28 without mitigations.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: Prior year audit qualified opinion due to pension fund audit issues; impact on 2024/25 opinion not yet determined
findings.detail: The auditor of the Teesside Pension Fund issued a disclaimed opinion for 2023/24. Although the council's prior year audit concluded on material accuracy of the pension liability, the auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence over the valuation of defined benefit assets, resulting in a qualified audit opinion. The impact on 2024/25 is being assessed.
findings.matters: Pension asset/liability valuations are material to the balance sheet; continued audit issues in this area could affect the council's reported financial position.
findings.figures: 2023/24 pension liability affected by asset ceiling; valuation amounts not finalised
findings.quote: Although we concluded on the material accuracy of the pension liability, we were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to conclude our work on the valuation of the defined benefit assets for the Council. As a result, we issued a qualified audit opinion for the Council to reflect this. We will need consider the impact of this on our 24/25 audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: MTFP shows £0.9m residual budget gap by 2027/28 even assuming full delivery of transformation savings
findings.detail: Unmitigated budget gaps total £7.1m (2025/26), £8.1m (2026/27), and £9m (2027/28). With transformation savings assumed, a balanced position is forecast for 2025/26 and 2026/27, but a £0.9m gap remains by 2027/28.
findings.matters: Even the council's best-case scenario leaves a residual structural deficit; this suggests budget pressures will persist beyond the MTFP.
findings.figures: Unmitigated gaps: £7.1m, £8.1m, £9m for 2025/26-2027/28. Residual gap £0.9m by 2027/28 after transformation savings.
findings.quote: Unmitigated gaps were reported of £7.1m in 2025/26, £8.1m in 2026/27 and £9m in 2027/28. However, an overall balanced position for 2025/26 and 2026/27 was reported assuming savings on transformation with a residual gap of £0.9m in 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: Powering Our Future transformation programme is critical to financial sustainability but has only identified £5.8m of £8.1m required savings
findings.detail: The transformation programme aims to deliver up to £8.1m of savings. To date, £5.8m has been identified from planned and approved schemes, leaving £2.3m still to be found. The council explicitly states it is critical this programme delivers to avoid further reliance on reserves.
findings.matters: The council's financial sustainability plan depends on successful delivery of transformation; if £2.3m of savings cannot be found, the budget gap widens further.
findings.figures: £8.1m target savings, £5.8m identified to 2026/27, £2.3m shortfall remaining
findings.quote: The Council's Powering Our Future Programme has identified significant opportunities to deliver services in a more efficient manner. The Programme has an ambition to deliver up to £8.1m of savings... The Powering Our Futures programme, and in particular the transformation mission has identified savings of £5.8m by 2026/27 to date (from planned and approved schemes). Work is ongoing to identify the remaining savings (£2.3m) required.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: Reserves being drawn down to cover deficits; council recognises this is unsustainable
findings.detail: The 2024/25 £7m overspend was funded from reserves. The council holds £28m useable reserves plus £8m general fund reserves. The auditor notes reserves have been decreasing over recent years and the council explicitly recognises that continued reserve use is not sustainable.
findings.matters: Using one-time reserves to cover recurring deficits is a depletion strategy, not a sustainable solution; it signals the budget gap is structural.
findings.figures: £7m overspend covered from reserves in 2024/25, £28m useable + £8m general fund reserves at 31 March 2025
findings.quote: The overspends reported in recent years have been largely covered by use of Council reserves. At 31 March 2025 reserves are reported as £28m useable and £8m general fund reserves. The Council recognises that continued use of reserves is not sustainable and is expecting this to be mitigated by the Powering Our Future projects.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: Cumulative DSG deficit of £6m forecast to reach £35m by 2027/28 when statutory override expires, risking inability to set balanced budget
findings.detail: The council has a £6m DSG deficit as at March 2025, forecast to grow to £35m by 2027/28. The statutory override allowing the DSG to be ring-fenced from the general fund expires on 31 March 2028. Without mitigations, the council will be unable to set a balanced budget at that point.
findings.matters: This creates a definitive financial cliff in three years that the council must address through its Delivering Better Value plan or face statutory breach.
findings.figures: £6m current deficit, £35m projected by 2027/28 without mitigations
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2025 the Council's DSG shows a cumulative deficit balance of £6m, which is forecasted to reach £35m by 2027/28 without mitigations. Although Government has signalled its intention to extend the period that the override covers to 31st March 2028, without action to address the cumulative deficit, at the end of this period there is a risk that the Council will be unable to set a balanced budget.

findings.paper_title: SBC - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 DRAFT FOR AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE 13.11.25
findings.headline: Children's Services overspend of £6m in 2024/25 is structural, with further overspends projected for 2025/26
findings.detail: Children's Services generated the council's largest overspend at £6m against budget in 2024/25. The council is forecasting continued overspends in 2025/26 due to persistent pressure in Children's and Adult Services. This overspend was covered from reserves.
findings.matters: This is not a one-off; it reflects ongoing structural demand and cost pressures in a major service area that cannot be quickly addressed.
findings.figures: £6m overspend 2024/25, £6.6m projected December 2024, £1.6m Q1 2025/26 pressures
findings.quote: The Council's largest overspend in 2024/25 was again seen in Children's Services of £6m against budget. It is currently forecasting an overspend in 2025/26 mainly owing to continued pressure in the Children's and Adult Services

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Mid Year Report 2025-26
findings.headline: £1.962m reserve established to cover potential unrealised losses on pooled investment funds if statutory override expires
findings.detail: The council has set aside a reserve to mitigate exposure to mark-to-market losses on £13.31m held in externally-managed property and other pooled funds, should the statutory accounting override not be extended beyond April 2029. This shows concern that investment asset values may fall.
findings.matters: A reserve set aside for a known downside risk (mark-to-market losses) suggests either poor liquidity in the investment portfolio or unease about asset valuations, and further erodes the council's discretionary reserves at a time when it is taking on significantly more debt.
findings.figures: £1.962m reserve; £13.31m pooled fund investments
findings.quote: The Authority has set up a reserve of £1.962m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended and unrealised losses on pooled investment funds are required to be recognised.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Mid Year Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Financing costs as proportion of revenue budget doubling from 2.3% to 4.6% in one year, then stabilizing at 5.0%
findings.detail: The annual charge to revenue for interest and minimum revenue provision on loans is forecast to rise from £4.3m (2.3% of net revenue stream) to £9.0m (4.6%), then £10.1m and £10.4m (both 5.0% of revenue). This represents a material and sustained increase in the annual cost of servicing debt, reducing flexibility for other council services.
findings.matters: A rising proportion of statutory revenue going to finance charges is a leading indicator of unsustainability; it crowds out service spending and reduces financial resilience, and signals either unsustainable capital plans or underlying revenue deficits being masked by borrowing.
findings.quote: Financing costs (£m) £4.3m £9.0m £10.1m £10.4m; Proportion of net revenue stream 2.3% 4.6% 5.0% 5.0%

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Mid Year Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Forecast new external borrowing surging to £97.1m annually by 2026/27, more than double the current trajectory
findings.detail: The liability benchmark forecast shows new borrowing of zero in 2024/25, rising to £37m in 2025/26, jumping to £97.1m in 2026/27 and £100.1m in 2027/28. This reflects capital expenditure forecast at £93.6m for 2025/26 but sustained high capital plans. Total debt is forecast to rise from £150.78m now to £250.63m by March 2028.
findings.matters: A rapid debt accumulation at a time of uncertain interest rates and constrained local government funding signals either major capital ambitions that may not be affordable, or an underlying structural deficit being funded by borrowing rather than solved.
findings.quote: Over the medium term it is estimated the authority, based on the current capital programme and the fact the authority has internally borrowed over the previous years will be required to undertake significant borrowing. In the higher rate environment that we are currently operating in this will mean higher costs of borrowing.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Strategy Mid Year Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Maturity structure breach: 51% of borrowing maturing within 12 months against a 25% limit
findings.detail: The council has breached its upper limit on short-term borrowing maturity, with 51.02% of the £127.48m debt portfolio maturing within 12 months. The council is deliberately holding short-term loans while waiting for longer-term interest rates to reduce, deliberately accepting refinancing risk.
findings.matters: Refinancing risk crystallises when rates unexpectedly rise or markets tighten, leaving the council unable to roll over maturing debt at affordable rates, forcing urgent borrowing at worse terms.
findings.figures: £127.48m total borrowing; 51.02% under 12 months vs 25% upper limit
findings.quote: Due to the strategy of only taking out short term loans the upper limit indicator for the percentage of total loans under 12 months was breached. Once longer-term interest rates reduce the authority will replace short term loans with longer term loans.

findings.paper_title: TM Outturn Report 2024-25
findings.headline: £18.322m in commercial property investments held pending future disposal decision; regulatory uncertainty on holding period
findings.detail: The council holds £18.322m in directly owned commercial property investments purchased before the 2021 CIPFA Prudential Code restricted borrowing for financial return. The council must review options for exiting these investments if an economic case exists. The statutory override currently protecting these holdings may extend to 2029 pending regulations, but provides no certainty and does not apply to new investments.
findings.matters: Uncertainty around future use of commercial investments creates potential liquidity need and signals possible future asset sales or write-downs, depending on property market recovery.
findings.figures: £18.322m in directly owned property investments; 2023-24 comparison £17.970m
findings.quote: The Authority currently holds £18.322m in commercial investments (2023-24 £17.970m) that were purchased prior to the change in the CIPFA Prudential Code. The Authority as part of the updated code in the future will need review the options for exiting these investments if there is an economical case to do so.

findings.paper_title: TM Outturn Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Net borrowing increased by £24.82m to £111.43m while usable reserves fell £17.35m, showing deteriorating financial position
findings.detail: The council's net borrowing position worsened substantially during the year, rising from £86.61m to £111.43m (28.6% increase). Total borrowing increased from £108.39m to £150.78m (up £42.39m), while usable reserves fell from £103.50m to £86.15m. The council remains under-borrowed by £35.94m against its capital financing requirement, but the overall trend shows declining financial headroom.
findings.matters: A sharp increase in net borrowing and decline in reserves indicates reduced financial resilience and increased reliance on borrowing, concerning lenders assessing the council's capacity to absorb financial shocks.
findings.figures: Net borrowing £111.43m (was £86.61m), increase £24.82m; total borrowing £150.78m (was £108.39m); usable reserves £86.15m (was £103.50m)
findings.quote: On 31st March 2025 the Council had net borrowing of £111.43m arising from its revenue and capital income and expenditure.

findings.paper_title: TM Outturn Report 2024-25
findings.headline: 43% of borrowing falls due within 12 months, breaching prudential indicator limit of 25% and creating refinancing risk
findings.detail: The council has shifted substantially to short-term borrowing (£61.38m in local authority loans with zero years weighted average maturity) as part of refinancing £21m of LOBO loans and preparing for other maturities. This breaches the prudential maturity structure upper limit and exposes the council to refinancing risk as these loans must be replaced, particularly concerning given short-term rates peaked at 6% in February-March 2025.
findings.matters: A breached maturity structure indicator signals elevated refinancing risk and vulnerability to interest rate spikes when loans come due for replacement.
findings.figures: £61.38m short-term local authority loans (0.0 years WAM); 43% of total borrowing under 12 months vs 25% limit; short-term rates reached 6% Feb-March 2025
findings.quote: Due to the strategy of only taking out short term loans the upper limit indicator for the percentage of total loans under 12 months was breached.

findings.paper_title: TM Outturn Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Accumulated DSG deficit of £6.7m creating ongoing cash drain and forcing council to borrow to cover education spending shortfall
findings.detail: The council has accumulated a £6.7m deficit on the Dedicated Schools Grant due to schools expenditure exceeding grant funding. The council must cash-flow this deficit and incurred borrowing costs of £300k in 2024-25 to cover it. Critically, these borrowing costs cannot be charged to DSG and must be absorbed by the general fund, creating a structural drain on council resources available for other services.
findings.matters: A growing DSG deficit signals that schools are consuming resources beyond their grant allocation, reducing the general fund's financial flexibility and creating a permanent cash drain.
findings.figures: £6.7m accumulated DSG deficit; £300k borrowing cost in year
findings.quote: At the end of the 2024/25 financial year the Council had an overall accumulative deficit of £6.7m on its DSG. The Council has to cash flow this deficit and any borrowing requirements and costs associated with borrowing incurred include this deficit. The cost of borrowing cannot be charged to the DSG under current regulations, so these are charged to the Councils general fund. The cost of this borrowing in year was up to £300k.

news_drafts.headline: Home to School Transport continues to escalate structurally, with no end to demand growth in sight.
news_drafts.lead: This is a recurring overspend in a growing area (demand-driven by SEND placement growth and transport costs). If demand continues to rise and costs escalate with provider pricing, this could become a material recurring pressure.

news_drafts.headline: Severe budget gaps ahead: £6.7m in 2026/27 rising to £18.4m by 2028/29.
news_drafts.lead: The scale and trajectory of these gaps raises questions about service sustainability without either significant borrowing, reserve drawdown, or council tax increases. A lender needs to understand the council's credible plan to address these gaps.
